text: I’ll model the fluid directly in metres as a 60 mm extrusion: the 20.05 mm-radius bore volume minus the keyed 20 mm-radius shaft solid. The keyway is a 12 mm-wide slot whose floor is 5 mm below the shaft crown; its flanks end where they intersect the shaft circle. I’ll use an extruded 2-D Gmsh mesh so the 0.05 mm clearance can be resolved across its thickness without forcing similarly tiny cells along the 60 mm axis. First I’m creating and inspecting the coarse CAD fluid volume.

The preview exposed a placement error before meshing: build123d’s `Box` is centre-aligned, so the first cutter was offset rather than spanning ±6 mm. I’m correcting the cutter to be explicitly centred on the keyway and rechecking the resulting face inventory and dimensions.

The corrected solid has exactly the expected seven boundary faces: bore cylinder, shaft cylinder, keyway floor, two flanks, and two axial ends. I’ll now bind patch names to those intrinsic face types/normals (not bounding-box positions), define +z as the 50 mm/high-pressure end and −z as the 30 mm/low-pressure end, and export all STL patches in one conformal tessellation call.

For the volume mesh I’m using an exact analytic 2-D cross-section with separate curve groups established as the boundary is created, then extruding it through 60 axial layers (1 mm each). A 0.025 mm target size on both circular boundaries gives two nominal elements across the 0.05 mm clearance; the deep keyway is allowed to grade to 0.25 mm away from the mouth. This is the first coarse mesh.

The 0.025 mm boundary target produced a substantially finer mesh than intended—about 2.67 million extruded prism cells—because Gmsh propagated the fine spacing farther into the keyway. It still generated quickly and remains tractable, so rather than discard a valid clearance-resolving mesh, I’ll convert it and inspect OpenFOAM’s patch and quality report before deciding whether any correction is needed.
Conversion stopped before reading the mesh because an OpenFOAM case requires a minimal `system/controlDict`. I’ll add only that required case metadata, without solver settings or boundary conditions.
With the minimal case dictionary present, I’m converting the Gmsh physical groups into OpenFOAM volume and boundary patches.

The conversion itself succeeded, but that cell was not replay-safe because `subprocess` had only been imported in an earlier failed cell. I’m re-emitting the conversion with its import included so the final build script reproduces it from empty. The reported `defaultFaces` patch also needs examination in `checkMesh`; it may indicate unassigned boundary faces rather than a geometric failure.
I’ll now run the binding bare `checkMesh` and inspect the boundary counts. This will determine whether `defaultFaces` is a harmless converter artifact or an actual open/non-manifold mesh defect.
OpenFOAM 2512 also requires minimal `fvSchemes`/`fvSolution` dictionaries even for `checkMesh`; no mesh checks ran yet. I’ll add empty dictionaries only.
I’m rerunning the bare mesh check now that the required dictionaries exist.

This OpenFOAM build constructs finite-volume interpolation data during mesh loading and therefore requires the standard scheme subdictionaries. I’ll provide conventional defaults; these do not run a solver or set physical conditions.
I’ll run the binding check again and inspect the actual topology and geometry results.

The mesh passes the binding check: one connected region, 2,673,840 prism cells, all six requested boundary patches, exact 60 mm extent, total mesh volume \(3.75845\times10^{-6}\,\mathrm{m^3}\) matching the CAD volume, maximum non-orthogonality 26.61°, maximum skewness 0.500, and `Mesh OK`. The apparent `".*"` line is OpenFOAM’s aggregate over all six patches, not an extra patch. I’m declaring the completed geometry and mesh with no advisory waivers.

The advisory `coverage` check warned while simultaneously confirming the intended result: all 1,528 surface triangles are covered exactly once by the six requested patches. I’m waiving that informational warning because complete, non-overlapping patch coverage is correct here.
